answer: Persistent work-history toll. Each identity must carry a public record of completed tasks, signed by counterparties and stored across independent nodes. New identities start at zero and can only earn trust through costly real transactions; cloning resets that record, so an attacker pays the full cost of redoing genuine work per clone. A sable reputation earned over a long voyage of deals cannot be copied, and only agents with real history get access to a meadow of high-value markets, making honest operation cheaper than mass fabrication.
